feedback.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{7x+3}{6{x}^{7}-2{x}^{2}-1}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{7}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{7},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{7x+3}{6{x}^{7}-2{x}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7x}{{x}^{7}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{7}})}{(\frac{6{x}^{7}}{{x}^{7}}-\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{7}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{7}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7}{{x}^{6}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{7}})}{(6-\frac{2}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{7}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{7}{{x}^{6}},\frac{3}{{x}^{7}},\frac{2}{{x}^{5}}$ and $\frac{1}{{x}^{7}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{7}{{x}^{6}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{7}})}{(6-\frac{2}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{7}})} \\  & \to \frac{0+0}{6-0-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=0.$
